editorial:
Imagine being a rich kid in LA with everything you could want, but you're still bored out of your mind. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow a group of wealthy teens who think the gang life looks cool and exciting from a distance. They decide to play a dangerous game by hanging out in rough neighborhoods and acting tough, thinking they are untouchable because of their parents' money. It starts off as a reckless adventure, but the vibe quickly shifts from a fun field trip to a nightmare when they realize that real criminals do not find their games funny.

What really hits home is how fast things spiral out of control once they provoke a violent gang. The acting feels natural, and you can really feel the panic as the kids realize they are in over their heads. While some parts of the story move a bit slow, the tension makes up for it. If you enjoy gritty dramas about bad choices, you should check this one out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you love owning your movies, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for a high-quality experience.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the gang decides to teach the rich kids a lesson they won't forget. After a series of threats and violence, the movie ends with a harsh reality check. You see the characters lose their innocence and safety as the violence catches up to them. There is no magical rescue; instead, it wraps up by showing that playing with fire always leads to getting burned, leaving the survivors traumatized and broken.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about rich people making terrible mistakes.
